newsitem.title: TURKEY: World Bank urges speedy privatisations for Turkey.
newsitem.headline: World Bank urges speedy privatisations for Turkey.

text.p: The World Bank said on Wednesday Turkey should implement a speedy and effective privatisation programme if it wanted to meet its ambitious revenue targets in the 1997 budget.

Jonathan Linn, the bank's Vice President for Europe and Central Asia, said in a statement there was a "need for effective and speedy implemantation of the privatisation program if the government's ambitious revenue targets for the 1997 budget are to be met."
Turkey aims to have a balanced budget and to raise at least $5.9 billion from privatisations in 1997.

Linn, who left Ankara on Wednesday after a five-day visit, said the World Bank, which has supported several infrastructure and structural projects in Turkey, would continue its financial backing if Turkey used the bank's funds effectively.

"An increase in bank support would depend on effective utilisation of funds already committed for projects in Turkey as well as on progress in addressing the structural problems which cause Turkey's chronic economic imbalances," he said.
The bank agreed in September to lend Ankara $5 million to finance a feasibility study for an oil pipeline from Azerbaijan's Baku to Turkey's southern port of Ceyhan.

Linn said he told Turkish officials the budgetary drain in this year's budget, which is expected to give a deficit of 1,300 trillion lira, would "become worse unless substantial corrective measures are taken" on social security and privatisation.
